meta.title: Cybersecurity: testing, auditing and response
meta.description: Penetration testing, code audits, hardening and incident response using OWASP, NIST and PTES. Always with written authorization and an agreed scope.

hero.title: We find your weaknesses before someone else does
hero.lead: Security testing, code review and incident response based on open methodologies, with authorization, an agreed scope and full transparency.

authorization.title: Every test requires written authorization
authorization.lead: This is the rule we do not negotiate: for ethical reasons, and because accessing a system without permission is a crime in most countries.
points: Before any test we sign an agreement that defines the assets included, the dates, the allowed techniques and the emergency contacts.
We only test systems that are yours or that you have the authority to authorize. We turn down requests to test third-party assets.
If your infrastructure runs on a cloud provider, we also comply with its security testing policies.
We do not act outside the agreed scope: if we find something relevant beyond it, we tell you without exploiting it.
authorization.disclosureText: Found a vulnerability in our own website?

scope.title: What we cover
scope.lead: Five services that can be hired separately.

pentest.title: Web and API penetration testing
pentest.text: Manual and automated testing of web applications, APIs and exposed services, following the OWASP testing guide and PTES.
includes: Injection, XSS, CSRF and business logic flaws

codeAudit.title: Code audit
codeAudit.text: Review of source code and dependencies to find design and implementation flaws that external testing cannot reach.

hardening.title: Hardening
hardening.text: Securing servers, containers, cloud and services: a smaller attack surface, least privilege and secure configuration.
includes: Reference to recognized guides such as the CIS Benchmarks

incident.title: Incident response
incident.text: Help to contain, investigate and recover from an incident, and to make sure it does not happen again.

training.title: Training
training.text: Hands-on training for developers and technical teams, and awareness for the rest of the organization.
includes: Practical workshops on the OWASP Top 10
Awareness of phishing and social engineering

outItems: Testing systems without the owner’s authorization
Denial-of-service attacks, unless expressly agreed and run in controlled environments
Social engineering of your staff without written agreement
Offensive activity against third parties, whatever the reason

methodologies.title: Open standards, not homemade recipes
methodologies.lead: We work with frameworks recognized across the industry so that results are comparable, reproducible and easy to understand.

owasp.name: OWASP
owasp.subtitle: WSTG · ASVS · Top 10
owasp.text: The reference for web application security testing and requirements. We use the Web Security Testing Guide as our testing guide, the ASVS as the verification criteria and the Top 10 to prioritize the most common risks.

nist.name: NIST
nist.subtitle: SP 800-115 · SP 800-61 · CSF · SSDF
nist.text: Guidance for technical security assessment (SP 800-115), incident handling (SP 800-61), risk governance (the Cybersecurity Framework) and secure software development (SSDF).

ptes.name: PTES
ptes.subtitle: Penetration Testing Execution Standard
ptes.text: A standard that structures a penetration test into seven phases, from pre-engagement to reporting, so that none gets skipped.

methodologies.scoringNote: We rate findings with CVSS and map them to CWE so you can prioritize and track them with your own tools.

phases.title: Seven phases, no shortcuts
phases.lead: This is how we structure a penetration test, following PTES.

items.title: Pre-engagement
items.text: We define the scope, the rules of engagement and the authorization.

items.title: Intelligence gathering
items.text: We identify assets, technologies and the exposed attack surface.

items.title: Threat modeling
items.text: We prioritize which assets matter and how they could be attacked.

items.title: Vulnerability analysis
items.text: We discover and validate weaknesses with tools and manual review.

items.title: Exploitation
items.text: We demonstrate real impact with the least intrusion necessary, always within scope.

items.title: Post-exploitation
items.text: We assess how far an attacker could get and remove any trace of our own.

items.title: Reporting
items.text: We deliver findings, evidence, risk and recommendations your team can act on.

cta.title: Want to put your defenses to the test?
cta.lead: Together we define the scope and we send you a proposal with authorization and clear timelines.
